evidence: Step 5b is EXEMPT BY DERIVATION, and the exemption is checked rather than asserted: data/Rdatasets.R sets `item = names(x)[i]` over the columns c(abany, abdefect, abnomore, abhlth, abpoor, abrape, absingle), so the item code is the source column name -- an identity bijection, with no positional assignment and no rename. The codes are also self-describing (abrape, abhlth, abpoor), so a permutation could not survive reading them. CORROBORATED NUMERICALLY against the GSS's own published marginals, which distinguishes every item from every other on both mapping axes. Live share of resp=1 (item_stats.R, n per item in parentheses) vs GSS published yes/(yes+no) over 1972-2024 from the gssrdoc counts-by-year tables: abhlth 89.6% (44,360) vs 89.79% [43,538/48,488]; abrape 81.4% (43,922) vs 81.71% [39,237/48,020]; abdefect 79.7% (44,152) vs 79.67% [38,428/48,234]; abpoor 47.2% (44,023) vs 48.15% [23,164/48,105]; abnomore 44.6% (44,072) vs 45.83% [22,063/48,140]; absingle 44.2% (44,020) vs 45.21% [21,745/48,103]; abany 41.4% (36,794) vs 43.32% [17,933/41,398]. Rank order is identical for all 7 and the largest discrepancy is 1.9 points, in the direction expected because the live port stops well short of 2024 while the published counts run to it. This simultaneously pins the option axis: resp=1 must be 'Yes', since the reversed reading would put abhlth at 10.4% where the GSS publishes 89.79%. WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH ON ITS OWN: the abnomore/absingle pair differ by only 0.4 points live (0.6 published), which is about 1 SE at these n, so the marginal route alone would leave that one pair PARTIAL; the identity bijection above is what separates them, and it distinguishes every item without appeal to any statistic.
